label: late-episode ramp; S2 state/previous S2 raise, low value raises, scaled by ramp
terms: (phase == D1) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 25.0) ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 25.0) ;; (phase == D2) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 25.0) ;; value * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 25.0) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 25.0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S2) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 25.0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 25.0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 25.0)
explanation: Raw GRU candidate n34 sits near -1 for most of the episode and climbs steeply over the last ~20 trials (timing alone R^2 0.90). Everything beyond timing is a modulation whose size grows with that ramp (all terms are multiplied by exp((ep_trial-99)/25)): a smooth within-decile ramp; reaching S2 raises it at D2, and having last reached S2 raises it at D1; a previous reward raises it at GO but lowers it at D1; lower model value raises it (value x ramp weight negative). Without the ramp scaling, the same history cues give only ~0.16 (dev). Observed-only version (value swapped for the last reward) gives 0.28 dev; with value 0.37 dev, 0.35 test, which is above the profile all-cue additive ceiling of 0.25 because of the ramp interaction. A large part of the late-episode variance is per-episode level differences (some episodes run high, others low across many trials) that these terms do not capture. No future variables used.
